title: He didn’t fall in the dark.
paragraphs:
He didn’t fall in the dark.
He fell in the fire.

Not alone.
Not far away.
Not gone.

Right there.
Close enough to see Jesus…
But far enough to deny Him.
Because some of us are not running from Christ.

We are just sitting in the wrong place…
warming our hands…
while our hearts grow cold.
Here’s the tension you don’t want to admit:
Peter did not wake up planning to deny Jesus.
But he stayed at a distance.
“Peter followed Him at a distance…” — Luke 22:54

Not with rebellion.
Not with hatred.
But with distance.

You still believe.
You still attend.
You still say the right things.
But your fire is no longer coming from Christ.
And that “somewhere else” is quietly shaping you.
Peter sat down by their fire.

Not the fire of devotion.
Not the fire of surrender.
But the fire of those who rejected Jesus.
And here is the terrifying truth:

You can sit in the wrong environment long enough…
and start sounding like it.

You can stay silent long enough…
and start agreeing with it.

You can crave approval long enough…
and start denying truth.

“She looked closely at him and said, ‘This man was with Him.’
But he denied it.” — Luke 22:56–57

A moment.
A question.
A chance to stand.
And Peter chose safety over truth.
How many times have we done the same?

Not with a shout…
but with silence.
You feel that nudge to speak for Christ…
You feel that conviction to stand…
Those words didn’t just leave Peter’s mouth.
They exposed what fear can do to a heart that has drifted.
Fear will make you betray what you once loved.
Fear will make you protect your reputation over your Redeemer.
Fear will make you forget who you are.
But here is the moment that breaks everything open:
“The Lord turned and looked at Peter…” — Luke 22:61

The prophecy.
The pride.
The failure.
The love he just denied.
“And he went out and wept bitterly.” — Luke 22:62
This is where most people misunderstand the story.
They think this is the end.
And repentance is where grace rushes in.
“I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail.” — Luke 22:32
Jesus didn’t say Peter wouldn’t fall.
He said his faith wouldn’t fail.
Because the grip of Christ is stronger than the failure of man.
This is where your story and Peter’s collide.
Because you may not be standing by a literal fire…
…but you know your version of it.
That relationship you know is pulling you away from God.
That hidden sin you keep justifying.
That environment where your faith goes silent.
But it is slowly training your heart to deny Christ.
Or do you do what Peter did?
Because here is the hope that changes everything:
After the resurrection, Jesus met him again.
And the man who once said, “I don’t know Him”…
would later stand and boldly proclaim Christ before thousands.
Your worst moment is not your final identity.
Your denial is not stronger than His grace.
Your distance is not greater than His pursuit.
But you cannot stay by that fire.
You cannot keep choosing comfort over Christ.
You cannot keep silencing your faith and expect your soul to stay alive.
Bring the version of you that you’re ashamed to admit exists.
And He still went to the cross.
“For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that He might bring us to God.” — 1 Peter 3:18
So step away from the wrong fire.
And come back to the One who never stopped loving you.
